copy.blurb:
Mexico face Korea Republic on Friday, overnight UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Korea Republic side, +12.1pp.

Public Elo rates Mexico 40 points higher than the other side (Mexico 1830, Korea Republic 1790). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Mexico to win at 40%, the draw at 28%, and Korea Republic to win at 32%. The away side reads 32% on this distribution — the model's central case for Korea Republic.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Mexico to win at 52%, the draw at 27%, and Korea Republic to win at 20%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Korea Republic side — 20% on the market, 32% on the engine, a +12.1pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Korea Republic the lower bound is 27%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +7.4pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 31 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Korea Republic are mispriced. Our number reads 32% on the away side; the market reads 20%. The +12.1pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Mexico v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
